> **TL;DR** — The agent has thirty tools and is told about about nineteen of them. `get_capabilities` — the one string an agent reads to learn what it can do — has not been updated since the tool set grew: it never mentions `compute_opportunity`, every `update_*` and `delete_*` tool, `get_evidence`, `delete_evidence`, or itself. Separately, the CLI has two whole command groups (`settings`, `profile`) that were written and never registered, and the terminal user cannot run `evaluate_outcome` — the only format checker in the codebase. After this issue there is **one generated description of what the system can do**, and the agent, the CLI, the docs, and the tests all read it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/core`, `area/cli` |
| **Priority** | `priority/medium` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | #83 (the tool set changes with the new required arguments) |
| **Related PRs** | #72 |
| **Blocks** | #96 |

---

## The problem

**1. `get_capabilities` is out of sync with the tool surface.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/messages.py:50-61` — `CAPABILITIES` describes:

> "🎯 **Manage Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)**: Add, list, and retrieve Jobs." — it does not mention that `update_job` and `delete_job` exist.
> "🗺️ **Build Job Maps**: Break down a Job into ordered Steps." — no mention of `update_step` / `delete_step`.
> "📊 **Track Desired Outcomes**" — no mention of `update_outcome` / `delete_outcome`.
> "📊 **Customer Outcomes**: Manage…" — no mention of `update_customer_outcome` / `delete_customer_outcome`.
> "🧾 **Evidence**" — names `add_evidence`, `list_evidence`, `promote_evidence` but not `get_evidence` or `delete_evidence`.
> `compute_opportunity` is never named. `get_capabilities` never names itself.

That is **11 of 30 tools invisible** to an agent that reads only this string.

**2. Nothing tests the sync.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py:14-142` — `ToolName` (30 values), `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, `TOOL_NAMES`. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py:16` asserts the live FastMCP registry's names equal `TOOL_SPECS` keys, and `:26-27` asserts the arguments and required names match. **The tool surface is protected. The human-readable description of it is not.** The only assertions on `CAPABILITIES` are substring checks in `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_odi.py:82-95` and `test_customer_outcomes.py:108`.

**3. The CLI deliberately allows drift, and does not use it.**
`tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py:40-41` asserts `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` keys equal a hardcoded 27-tool set and that the set is a **subset** of `TOOL_NAMES` — so the CLI is permitted to omit tools. It omits three: `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_framework_guidelines`, `get_capabilities`. A terminal-only user — which the README makes a first-class path, with a binary installer and 24-hour auto-update — has **no access to the only format validator in the codebase**.

**4. Two CLI command groups were written and never registered.**
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/settings.py:11-21` — `settings_app` and its `flags_app` sub-app. `grep add_typer` across `apps/cli/src/` returns only `cli.py:29-40` and `settings.py:21`. **`agentic-odi settings flags list` does not exist.**
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/profile.py:13` — `app = typer.Typer(name="profile")` is never registered. There is no `agentic-odi profile` command, and no `agentic-odi setup` command either.
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/onboard.py:264` — the onboarding card tells the user to *"Run `agentic-odi setup` to configure your product baseline interactively."* **That command does not exist.**

**5. The first-run onboarding never fires.**
`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/onboard.py:233-264` — `maybe_run_first_launch()` is called only from `apps/cli/tests/test_onboard.py`. It is never called from `cli.py`. The card a real user is told to expect never appears.

**6. The URL-based inference is a stub.**
`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/onboard.py:166-170` — `primary_user`, `business_model`, `core_problem`, and `current_focus` are hardcoded `None` with the comment `# (placeholder: derive from title tokens)`. `infer_baseline` (`:70-99`) produces an all-`None` baseline except the domain and a confidence value.

**7. Three of the four feature flags are read by nothing.**
`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/flags.py` defines `experimental_connectors`, `auto_update`, `advanced_metrics`, and `developer_mode`. Only `auto_update` is consulted (`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/update.py:243`). `experimental_connectors` gates nothing — the connectors feature is fully live. `advanced_metrics` and `developer_mode` gate nothing at all.

**8. The CLI's remote-backend parsing is string sniffing.**
`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:545-559` — `_parse_remote` treats a response as an error if the text starts with `"Error:"` or contains `" not found:"`, and `_extract_json` (`:562-569`) finds the first `{` or `[` and parses the tail. This works by accident of formatting. See #91 for the studio-side equivalent.

## What a person experiences

An agent asks the MCP server *"what can you do?"* and gets back a complete, accurate, machine-readable inventory of every tool, with its arguments, whether they are required, and what they change. It never has to guess. A person in a terminal types `agentic-odi` and gets the same inventory, plus a `settings` group that actually works and the `setup` command the onboarding card already promised. A person who asks the agent to check an outcome statement before saving it can do that from the terminal with one command.

## Specification

### 7.1 A generated manifest

Add to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`:

```python
class ToolEffect(StrEnum):
    READ = "read"
    WRITE = "write"
    DESTRUCTIVE = "destructive"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolSpec:
    name: str
    summary: str                  # one line, human-readable
    effect: ToolEffect
    arguments: tuple[str, ...]
    required: tuple[str, ...]
    returns: str                  # one line
    stage: str | None = None      # ODI stage this tool belongs to, e.g. "2"
```

Every one of the 30 existing tools gets a `summary`, an `effect`, and a `returns` line. `TOOL_SPECS` becomes the single source of truth.

Add:

```python
def capability_manifest() -> dict:
    """A complete, generated description of the tool surface."""

def capability_summary() -> str:
    """The human-readable rendering, used by get_capabilities."""
```

`capability_summary()` groups by `effect` and by ODI stage and names **every** tool. It must not be hand-written.

### 7.2 `get_capabilities` returns the manifest

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:256` — the `get_capabilities` tool returns `capability_manifest()` (the JSON), not the hardcoded `CAPABILITIES` string.

### 7.3 A drift test that cannot lie

Add `packages/core/tests/test_capability_manifest.py`:

- every name in `TOOL_SPECS` appears in `capability_summary()`;
- every name in `TOOL_SPECS` appears in `capability_manifest()["tools"]`;
- the manifest and the live FastMCP registry have the same names (this already exists as `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py:16` — keep it, and extend it to the new tool);
- every tool has a non-empty `summary`, `effect`, and `returns`;
- `effect` is derived from the name where the name is unambiguous (`get_*`/`list_*` → `READ`, `delete_*` → `DESTRUCTIVE`, everything else → `WRITE`) and **the derivation is asserted**, so a tool cannot be accidentally marked read-only;

### 7.4 The CLI reads the same manifest

- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py` — add a `capabilities` command group: `agentic-odi capabilities` (human table), `agentic-odi capabilities --json` (the manifest), `agentic-odi capabilities tools` (names only).
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:460-488` — add the missing local handlers so the CLI can reach every tool:
  - `_evaluate_outcome` → `evaluate_outcome`
  - `_get_odi_framework_guidelines` → `get_odi_framework_guidelines`
  - `_get_capabilities` → `get_capabilities`
  - `_get_odi_schema` → `get_odi_schema`
  - and any tool added by #79, #80, #82, #85.
- `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py:40-41` — **tighten the assertion**: the local handler set must now **equal** `TOOL_NAMES`, not be a subset. This is the single most valuable line in the issue: it converts a documented drift allowance into a hard invariant. Every new tool must then be reachable from the terminal.
- Add a CLI command for the format checker:
  - `agentic-odi desired-outcomes evaluate "<statement>"` — runs `evaluate_outcome` and prints the verdict, the issues, and the suggestions. **This is the first terminal access to the validator in the project's history.**
- Add `agentic-odi schema` (already declared at `cli.py:155` — verify it works) and make it print the manifest's schema for every entity.

### 7.5 Register the orphan CLI groups

- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py:29-41` — register:
  - `settings_app` from `settings.py:11` → `agentic-odi settings` and `agentic-odi settings flags` (the flags group with `list`, `get`, `set`, `reset`).

- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/onboard.py:233-264` — call `maybe_run_first_launch()` from `cli.py` on first launch, behind the `developer_mode` flag or an explicit `--onboard` flag, so the card actually appears.

[{"body":"## Summary

The first visit no longer opens on a four-step modal. The studio opens on one question — **What do you want to win?** — with the composer focused, and the tour is something you ask for. Guidance replaces the dialog: after the first exchange, at most one quiet line above the composer suggests the next useful thing.

Rebuilt from #132 on current `main`. Its rendered-site commit is gone (`main` no longer tracks `website/dist`), and its collisions with the assistant-ui runtime are resolved in the runtime's favour.

## What changed

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/studio/src/App.tsx` path | No auto-open. The stage renders the conversation first; the wizard only mounts when the provider opens it. |
| `onboarding/machine.ts` | `shouldAutoOpen` is deleted. The tour moves only when the provider asks it to; `openTour` resumes stored progress and `restart` starts from the top. |
| `onboarding/OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Opens closed, persists only once the tour is actually opened or finished, and exposes `openTour`. |
| `lib/guidance.ts`, `components/chat/GuidanceHint.tsx` | One hint at a time, chosen from the canvas: add context before you have any, capture the evidence a score is missing after. Silent before the first exchange, above the composer rather than over the thread, and dismissible permanently. |
| `chat/Hero.tsx` | A first run holds a single invitation and does not rotate; **Show me around** opens the tour when the flag is on. The starter pills still come from the assistant-ui runtime. |
| `lib/greeting.ts` | "What do you want to win?" is the first candidate, and the first-run path keeps it still. |
| `components/SettingsPanel.tsx`, `features/flags.ts` | "Replay the tour", described as opt-in. The flag keeps its name (`firstRunWizard`) so existing settings keep working. |
| docs | `README.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/roadmap.md`, plus the design note under `docs/superpowers/specs/`. |

## What this does not do

- **No new onboarding content.** The four steps, their copy, and their goals are unchanged; only when they open changed.
- **The flag keeps its name.** `firstRunWizard` still gates the tour, because renaming it would silently turn the tour off for anyone who set it and break the storage key.
- **No pill rework.** The branch's older "Pressure-test a bet" fallback pill is dropped; the runtime owns the starters now, and the remaining shortcut is **Opportunity landscape**, as on `main`.
- **No rendered site is committed.** The original branch's `website/dist` commit is dropped; the site is built in CI from source.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest -q                        1160 passed
uv run --directory website pytest tests/  250 passed
uv run ruff check .                     All checks passed
uv run ruff format --check .            287 files already formatted
uv run mypy apps brand packages         Success: no issues found in 162 source files
npm run lint (apps/studio)              0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings)
npm run typecheck (apps/studio)         clean
npm test -- --run (apps/studio)         422 passed (49 files)
npm run build (apps/studio)             built
```

`ChatStage.test.tsx` now stubs the onboarding context, the same way it stubs the studio state: the stage is rendered without the shell there, so the tour stays off, and the onboarding flow has its own suite.

         for line in block.splitlines():

                 name = line[len("event: ") :]

     def _apply_event(self, ev: Event) -> None:
         et = ev["type"]
         p = ev["payload"]
         if et == "JOB_CREATED":
             self.jobs[p["id"]] = Job.model_validate(p)
         elif et == "STEP_CREATED":
             self.steps[p["id"]] = Step.model_validate(p)
         elif et == "OUTCOME_CREATED":
             self.outcomes[p["id"]] = Outcome.model_validate(p)
         elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_CREATED":
             self.customer_outcomes[p["id"]] = CustomerOutcome.model_validate(p)
         elif et == "EVIDENCE_CREATED":
             self.evidence[p["id"]] = Evidence.model_validate(p)
         elif et == "JOB_UPDATED":
             self._merge_updates(self.jobs, p, Job)
         elif et == "STEP_UPDATED":
             self._merge_updates(self.steps, p, Step)
         elif et == "OUTCOME_UPDATED":
             self._merge_updates(self.outcomes, p, Outcome)
         elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED":
             self._merge_updates(self.customer_outcomes, p, CustomerOutcome)
         elif et == "JOB_DELETED":
             job_id = p["id"]

                 del self.steps[key]
             for key in [k for k, v in self.outcomes.items() if v.job_id == job_id]:
                 del self.outcomes[key]
             for key in [k for k, v in self.customer_outcomes.items() if v.job_id == job_id]:
                 del self.customer_outcomes[key]
             for key in [

                 for k, v in self.evidence.items()
                 if v.job_id == job_id
                 or (v.step_id is not None and v.step_id not in self.steps)
                 or (v.outcome_id is not None and v.outcome_id not in self.outcomes)
             ]:
                 del self.evidence[key]
         elif et == "STEP_DELETED":
             step_id = p["id"]
             self.steps.pop(step_id, None)
             for key in [k for k, v in self.outcomes.items() if v.step_id == step_id]:
                 del self.outcomes[key]
             for key in [k for k, v in self.customer_outcomes.items() if v.step_id == step_id]:

             for key in [

display.text:
"""Evaluate desired-outcome statements against the ODI format."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

_CONTEXT_MARKERS = (
    " when ",
    " while ",
    " before ",
    " after ",
    " during ",
    " if ",
    " as ",
)

_VAGUE_TERMS = ("better", "improve", "optimize", "faster", "easier")


def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return format feedback for a desired-outcome statement."""
    text = statement.strip()
    lowered = text.lower()
    padded = f" {lowered} "
    issues: list[str] = []
    suggestions: list[str] = []

    direction: str | None = None
    if lowered.startswith("minimize"):
        direction = "minimize"
    elif lowered.startswith("maximize"):
        direction = "maximize"
    else:
        issues.append("Statement must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.")
        suggestions.append("Start with 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] ...'.")

    if " the " not in padded:
        issues.append("Name the object of control after 'the'.")
        suggestions.append("Say what is being minimized or maximized, e.g. 'the time to ...'.")

    if not any(marker in padded for marker in _CONTEXT_MARKERS):
        issues.append("Add the execution context with 'when ...', 'while ...', or 'before ...'.")
        suggestions.append("Close with the situation, e.g. '... when onboarding a new customer'.")

    if len(text.split()) < 4:
        issues.append("Statement is too short to describe a measurable outcome.")
        suggestions.append("Describe the metric, the object, and the context.")

    if len(text) > 200:
        issues.append("Statement is longer than 200 characters; keep it to one measurable outcome.")
        suggestions.append("Split broad statements into separate outcomes.")

    vague = [term for term in _VAGUE_TERMS if term in lowered]
    if vague:
        issues.append(f"Replace vague terms with a measurable metric: {', '.join(vague)}.")
        suggestions.append("Use a metric such as time, cost, effort, errors, or likelihood.")

    return {
        "statement": text,
        "valid": not issues,
        "direction": direction,
        "issues": issues,
        "suggestions": suggestions,
    }

"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field


class Direction(str, Enum):
    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"


class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
    RETENTION = "retention"
    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
    OTHER = "other"


def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))


class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")


class Step(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")


class Outcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
    statement: str = Field(
        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
    )
    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
    )
    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
    )


class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
    name: str
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    object_of_control: str
    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
    statement: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
    category: BusinessImpactCategory
    statement: str
    detail: str | None = None
    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


EvidenceItemType = Literal["catalog", "resource", "tool_result", "manual", "note"]


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    """A captured research record linked (optionally) to ODI artifacts."""

    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    source_name: str = Field(..., description="Connector or person that produced the record")
    source_kind: str = Field(..., description="Connector kind, e.g. mcp, rest, webhook, manual")
    item_type: EvidenceItemType = Field(
        "manual", description="Normalized record kind produced by the connector"
    )
    name: str = Field(..., description="Short human-readable label for the record")
    content: str = Field(..., description="Normalized text content of the record")
    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Original record payload")
    job_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job this evidence supports")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job-map Step this evidence supports")
    outcome_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Desired Outcome this evidence supports")


class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
    )
    customer_value: CustomerValue
    business_value: BusinessValue

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT = """You are an expert in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI). Your purpose is to help users discover, define, and prioritize high-value jobs, desired outcomes, and opportunities."""

ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = """## Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) — Stage-by-Stage Tool Guide

Follow this sequence when guiding a user through the ODI process:

### Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)
- **When**: Always start here if no Job exists.
- **Ask the user**: 'What is the main task or goal your customer is trying to accomplish?'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_job(name, description)` — Create the Job once identified.
  - `get_jobs()` — Check if a relevant Job already exists before creating a new one.
  - `get_job(job_id)` — Retrieve details of a specific existing Job.

### Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes
- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
- **Outcome statement format**: 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] when [context].'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.
  - `evaluate_outcome(statement, job_id?)` — Check that a statement starts with Minimize/Maximize, names a metric, and states its context before saving it.

### Stage 3: Calculate Opportunity Scores
- **When**: After outcomes have importance and satisfaction scores.
- **Formula**: Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)
- **Scores > 10** indicate high innovation opportunity. Guide the user to focus efforts there.
- **Tools to use**: `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review opportunity_score field on each outcome.

### Stage 4: Build the Job Map
- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Use to organize the job execution context.
- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_step(job_id, name, order)` — Add each chronological step.
  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map.

### Supporting Tools
- `add_evidence(...)` / `list_evidence(job_id?)` — Attach customer research records from connectors to a Job, Step, or Outcome without altering the ODI artifacts.
- `promote_evidence(evidence_id, target, job_id?)` — Turn a captured record into a Job or desired Outcome when it is ready.
- `get_odi_schema()` — Return the canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity.

### General Rule
Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), and always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 4)."""

"""Evaluate desired-outcome statements against the ODI format.

The single authority for what a well-formed desired-outcome statement looks
like. Every write path (service, MCP tool, CLI, Studio API) routes through
``evaluate_outcome_statement`` / ``require_outcome_statement`` so the store
only ever contains methodologically sound data.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

_CONTEXT_MARKERS = (
    " when ",
    " while ",
    " before ",
    " after ",
    " during ",
    " if ",
    " as ",
)

_SOLUTION_NOUNS = (
    "notification",
    "dashboard",
    "button",
    "feature",
    "screen",
    "email",
    "workflow",
    "integration",
    "report",
    "toggle",
)

_VAGUE_TERMS = ("better", "improve", "optimize", "faster", "easier")

_MIN_WORDS = 6
_MAX_CHARS = 200

_DIRECTIONS = ("minimize", "maximize")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StatementIssue:
    """A single validation problem with a statement."""

    code: str
    message: str
    suggestion: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StatementVerdict:
    """The result of evaluating a desired-outcome statement."""

    valid: bool
    direction: str | None
    unit_of_measure: str | None
    object_of_control: str | None
    contextual_clarifier: str | None
    issues: tuple[StatementIssue, ...]


class OutcomeStatementError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a statement fails the ODI format check.

    The message is actionable: it says what is wrong and what to do about it.
    """

    def __init__(self, verdict: StatementVerdict) -> None:
        self.verdict = verdict
        lines = [f"Outcome statement is not valid: {verdict.direction or ''}".strip()]
        for issue in verdict.issues:
            lines.append(f"- {issue.message}")
            if issue.suggestion:
                lines.append(f"  Fix: {issue.suggestion}")
        super().__init__("\n".join(lines))


def _detect_direction(text: str) -> str | None:
    lowered = text.lower()
    for direction in _DIRECTIONS:
        if lowered.startswith(direction):
            return direction
    return None


def _find_unit_of_measure(text: str) -> str | None:
    lowered = text.lower()
    units = (
        "time",
        "cost",
        "number",
        "frequency",
        "rate",
        "percentage",
        "time to",
        "steps",
        "attempts",
        "likelihood",
        "duration",
        "errors",
    )
    for unit in units:
        if f" {unit} " in f" {lowered} " or lowered.startswith(f"{unit} ") or lowered.endswith(f" {unit}"):
            return unit
    # Any digit present implies a measurable unit.
    import re

    if re.search(r"\d", text):
        return "number"
    return None


def _find_object_of_control(text: str) -> str | None:
    padded = f" {text.lower()} "
    if " the " in padded:
        return "the"
    return None


def _find_contextual_clarifier(text: str) -> str | None:
    padded = f" {text.lower()} "
    for marker in _CONTEXT_MARKERS:
        if marker in padded:
            return marker.strip()
    return None


def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> StatementVerdict:
    """Return a :class:`StatementVerdict` for a desired-outcome statement."""
    text = statement.strip()
    lowered = text.lower()
    padded = f" {lowered} "
    issues: list[StatementIssue] = []

    direction = _detect_direction(text)
    if direction is None:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="missing_direction",
                message="Statement must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.",
                suggestion="Start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize', e.g. 'Minimize the time it takes to...'.",
            )
        )

    unit_of_measure = _find_unit_of_measure(text)
    if unit_of_measure is None:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="missing_unit",
                message="Statement must contain a unit of measure (time, cost, number, frequency, rate, percentage, steps, attempts, or a digit).",
                suggestion="Add a unit of measure, e.g. 'time', 'cost', or 'number of …'.",
            )
        )

    object_of_control = _find_object_of_control(text)
    if object_of_control is None:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="missing_object",
                message="Statement must name an object of control after 'the'.",
                suggestion="Name the object, e.g. 'the time it takes to …'.",
            )
        )

    contextual_clarifier = _find_contextual_clarifier(text)
    if contextual_clarifier is None:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="missing_context",
                message="Statement must state when it happens (when, while, before, after, during, if, as).",
                suggestion="Add when it happens, e.g. '… when onboarding'.",
            )
        )

    word_count = len(text.split())
    if word_count < _MIN_WORDS:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="too_short",
                message=f"Statement is too short ({word_count} words); needs at least {_MIN_WORDS}.",
                suggestion="Describe the metric, the object, and the context.",
            )
        )

    if len(text) > _MAX_CHARS:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="too_long",
                message=f"Statement is longer than {_MAX_CHARS} characters; keep it to one measurable outcome.",
                suggestion="Split broad statements into separate outcomes.",
            )
        )

    vague = [term for term in _VAGUE_TERMS if term in lowered]
    if vague:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="vague_term",
                message=f"Replace vague terms with a measurable metric: {', '.join(vague)}.",
                suggestion="Use a metric such as time, cost, effort, errors, or likelihood.",
            )
        )

    solution_found = [noun for noun in _SOLUTION_NOUNS if f" {noun} " in padded]
    if solution_found:
        issues.append(
            StatementIssue(
                code="solution_framed",
                message=f"Statement names a solution ({', '.join(solution_found)}), not a customer problem.",
                suggestion="Name the customer's problem instead of a feature or product.",
            )
        )

    return StatementVerdict(
        valid=not issues,
        direction=direction,
        unit_of_measure=unit_of_measure,
        object_of_control=object_of_control,
        contextual_clarifier=contextual_clarifier,
        issues=tuple(issues),
    )


def require_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> StatementVerdict:
    """Validate a statement and raise :class:`OutcomeStatementError` if invalid."""
    verdict = evaluate_outcome_statement(statement)
    if not verdict.valid:
        raise OutcomeStatementError(verdict)
    return verdict


def statement_to_dict(verdict: StatementVerdict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Render a verdict as the legacy dict shape for MCP/CLI serialization."""
    return {
        "statement": "",
        "valid": verdict.valid,
        "direction": verdict.direction,
        "issues": [issue.message for issue in verdict.issues],
        "suggestions": [
            issue.suggestion for issue in verdict.issues if issue.suggestion is not None
        ],
        "unit_of_measure": verdict.unit_of_measure,
        "object_of_control": verdict.object_of_control,
        "contextual_clarifier": verdict.contextual_clarifier,
    }

     self._last_event_id = 0
     for ev in self.store.get_stream(workspace_id=self._workspace_id, replay_order=True):
         self._apply_event(ev)
 
+def _backfill_legacy_outcomes(self) -> None:
+    """One-time migration: backfill null scores on legacy outcomes.
+
+    Assigns importance=5.0, satisfaction=5.0 to any outcome missing either
+    score, records an OUTCOME_BACKFILLED event per outcome, and marks the
+    repository as backfilled so reloads do not repeat the migration.
+    """
+    if self._backfilled:
+        return
+    needs_backfill = [
+        o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.importance is None or o.satisfaction is None
+    ]
+    if not needs_backfill:
+        self._backfilled = True
+        return
+    for outcome in needs_backfill:
+        updates: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        if outcome.importance is None:
+            updates["importance"] = 5.0
+        if outcome.satisfaction is None:
+            updates["satisfaction"] = 5.0
+        updates["opportunity_score"] = compute_opportunity_score(
+            updates.get("importance", outcome.importance),
+            updates.get("satisfaction", outcome.satisfaction),
+        )
+        self.store.append(
+            "OUTCOME_BACKFILLED",
+            {"id": outcome.id, "updates": updates},
+            workspace_id=self._workspace_id,
+            device_id=self._device_id,
+        )
+    self._sync()
+    self._backfilled = True
+
 def _sync(self) -> None:
     for ev in self.store.get_stream(workspace_id=self._workspace_id):
         if ev["id"] > self._last_event_id:
             self._apply_event(ev)

input.newString:
ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = """## Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) — Stage-by-Stage Tool Guide

Follow this sequence when guiding a user through the ODI process:

### Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)
- **When**: Always start here if no Job exists.
- **Ask the user**: 'What is the main task or goal your customer is trying to accomplish?'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_job(name, description)` — Create the Job once identified.
  - `get_jobs()` — Check if a relevant Job already exists before creating a new one.
  - `get_job(job_id)` — Retrieve details of a specific existing Job.

### Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes
- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
- **Outcome statement format**: `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`, e.g. 'Minimize the time it takes to onboard a new engineer.'
- **Direction**: Must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.
- **Unit of measure**: A measurable unit (time, cost, number, frequency, rate, percentage, steps, attempts).
- **Object of control**: The thing being acted on (named after 'the').
- **Contextual clarifier**: When it happens (when, while, before, after, during, if, as).
- **Scores**: Both `importance` and `satisfaction` are required (1–10). An outcome without them cannot be compared to anything.
- **Expectation**: Qualitative interviews typically uncover 50–150 desired outcome statements.
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.
  - `evaluate_outcome(statement, job_id?)` — **Pre-write check**: run this before `add_outcome` to confirm the statement matches the ODI format. It returns coded issues and suggestions for any failure.
  - `update_outcome(outcome_id, ...)` — Correct a statement or scores; the same validation applies.

### Stage 3: Build the Job Map
- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Never build a map on a job with zero outcomes — outcomes are what give the steps their meaning.
- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
- **Eight Universal Job Map stages** (in order): Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude.
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_step(job_id, name, order, stage?)` — Add each chronological step; `stage` must be one of the eight stages above, and `stage_index` is derived from it.
  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map, ordered by stage.

### Stage 4: Calculate Opportunity Scores
- **When**: After outcomes have importance and satisfaction scores.
- **Formula**: Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)
- **Scores > 10** indicate high innovation opportunity. Guide the user to focus efforts there.
- **Scores ≤ 10** indicate appropriately served or overserved outcomes.
- **Tools to use**: `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review opportunity_score field on each outcome. `compute_opportunity(importance, satisfaction)` — Calculate a score directly.

### Stage 5: Segment by Underserved Outcomes
- **When**: After outcomes are scored.
- **Never** segment by demographics. A segment is a group of people plus a functional job.
- **Tools**: `get_segments(job_id?)`, `propose_strategy()`.
- A segment is underserved when one of its outcomes scores above 10, and overserved when the customer already has the outcome (satisfaction at or above importance).

### Stage 6: Formulate the Innovation Strategy
- **When**: After segments are clear.
- **Differentiated**: improve an existing product for an underserved segment.
- **Disruptive**: offer a lower-cost solution to an overserved segment.
- **New-Market**: create for a job no one is being served on today.
- **Tools**: `propose_strategy(job_id?)`.
- Always state the strategies you rejected and why.

### General Rule
Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 3), and always score outcomes (Stage 2) before computing opportunity (Stage 4). If a tool rejects a write, read the message, fix the statement or the numbers, and try once. Do not retry the same call unchanged."""


def get_odi_framework_guidelines() -> str:
    return ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES

- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
- **Outcome statement format**: 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] when [context].'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.

### Stage 4: Build the Job Map
- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Use to organize the job execution context.
- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
- **Tools to use**:
  - `add_step(job_id, name, order)` — Add each chronological step.
  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map.

### Supporting Tools
- `add_evidence(...)` / `list_evidence(job_id?)` — Attach customer research records from connectors to a Job, Step, or Outcome without altering the ODI artifacts.
- `promote_evidence(evidence_id, target, job_id?)` — Turn a captured record into a Job or desired Outcome when it is ready.
- `get_odi_schema()` — Return the canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity.

### General Rule
Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), and always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 4)."""


def get_odi_framework_guidelines() -> str:
    return ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES

display.text:
"""HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.

Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::

    {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
               "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}

The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"

#: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
#: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")

STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
    StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
    StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
    StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
    StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
    StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
}

CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
    400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
    409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
    422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
    500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
    502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
}


class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
    """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""

    def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
        self.error = error
        self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
        super().__init__(error.message)


def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
    """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
    return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)


def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:
    """Return the error code that belongs to an HTTP status."""
    return CODE_FOR_STATUS.get(status_code, StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL)


def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
    """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
    return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")


def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    if not error.request_id:
        error = error.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id})
    return {"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}


def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
    return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)


def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a :class:`StudioHTTPError` as the one error body."""
    return _error_response(request, exc.error, exc.status_code)


def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
    detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
        message="Request validation failed.",
        detail=detail,
        suggestion="Check the request body and try again.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 422)


def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:
    parts: list[str] = []
    for error in exc.errors():
        location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
        parts.append(f"{location}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def http_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    """Render a Starlette/FastAPI ``HTTPException`` as the one error body."""
    error = StudioError(
        code=code_for_status(exc.status_code),
        message=str(exc.detail),
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, exc.status_code)


def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    """Log an unexpected failure and return it without internals."""
    request_id = request_id_for(request)
    logger.exception("unhandled studio-api error (request_id=%s)", request_id, exc_info=exc)
    error = StudioError(
        code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
        message="Something went wrong. The team has been notified.",
    )
    return _error_response(request, error, 500)


def _safe_request_id(candidate: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the client's request id when it is safe to echo, else a fresh one."""
    if candidate and REQUEST_ID_PATTERN.match(candidate):
        return candidate
    return uuid4().hex


class RequestIdMiddleware:
    """Accept or mint an ``X-Request-ID`` and echo it on the response."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        request_id = _safe_request_id(Headers(scope=scope).get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER))
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id

        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                MutableHeaders(scope=message)[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = request_id
            await send(message)

        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)


def register_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Install the one-error-body handlers on an app."""
    handler: Any = studio_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StudioHTTPError, handler)
    handler = validation_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, handler)
    handler = http_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, handler)
    handler = unhandled_error_handler
    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, handler)

display.text:
"""Error types for Agentic ODI operations.

Every failure mode in the domain has a dedicated exception class so callers
can branch on the *kind* of failure instead of matching on message text. All
ODI errors inherit from :class:`OdiError`, so a single ``except OdiError``
catches anything this package raises deliberately.

Note that :class:`ValidationError` here is the *ODI contract* error. Pydantic's
own ``ValidationError`` remains available from ``pydantic`` and is unrelated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class OdiError(Exception):
    """Base class for every deliberate Agentic ODI failure."""


class ValidationError(OdiError, ValueError):
    """Input did not satisfy the ODI contract.

    Also a :class:`ValueError` so that callers written against the previous
    behaviour (which raised bare ``ValueError``) keep working unchanged.
    """


class NotFoundError(OdiError):
    """A referenced resource does not exist.

    ``hint`` is an optional sentence telling the caller what to do next. It is
    appended to the message so it survives into user-facing output.
    """

    def __init__(self, resource_id: str, kind: str, hint: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.resource_id = resource_id
        self.kind = kind
        self.hint = hint or ""
        message = f"{kind} not found: {resource_id}"
        if self.hint:
            message = f"{message}. {self.hint}"
        super().__init__(message)


class ConflictError(OdiError):
    """The requested change conflicts with the current state."""


class RateLimitError(OdiError):
    """The caller exceeded an allowed rate or volume."""

    def __init__(
        self, message: str = "Rate limit exceeded", retry_after: float | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        super().__init__(message)


class ConsentRequired(OdiError):
    """The agent tried to act on the workspace before the PM agreed to it."""


class StoreError(OdiError):
    """The persistence layer could not complete the operation."""


class SerializationError(OdiError):
    """A payload could not be converted to or from its wire format."""


_STATUS_BY_ERROR: tuple[tuple[type[OdiError], int], ...] = (
    (ValidationError, 400),
    (NotFoundError, 404),
    (ConflictError, 409),
    (RateLimitError, 429),
    (ConsentRequired, 403),
    (StoreError, 500),
    (SerializationError, 502),
)


def error_status(err: OdiError) -> int:
    """Map an ODI error onto the HTTP status code that best describes it.

    Unknown :class:`OdiError` subclasses fall back to ``500`` rather than
    raising, so a new error type can never break an error handler.
    """
    for error_type, status in _STATUS_BY_ERROR:
        if isinstance(err, error_type):
            return status
    return 500

"""Tests for the SQLite-backed repository and its event-sourced snapshot."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

import pytest
from agentic_odi_core.models import (
    BusinessImpactCategory,
    BusinessValue,
    CustomerOutcome,
    CustomerValue,
    Direction,
    Evidence,
    Job,
    Outcome,
    Step,
)
from agentic_odi_core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository


def _customer_outcome(job_id: str, *, outcome_id: str = "co-1") -> CustomerOutcome:
    return CustomerOutcome(
        id=outcome_id,
        job_id=job_id,
        customer_value=CustomerValue(
            direction=Direction.MINIMIZE,
            unit_of_measure="minutes",
            object_of_control="time to onboard",
            statement="Minimize the time it takes to onboard",
            importance=8.0,
            satisfaction=4.0,
        ),
        business_value=BusinessValue(
            category=BusinessImpactCategory.REVENUE_GROWTH,
            statement="Increase expansion revenue",
        ),
    )


def test_add_and_read_back_every_entity(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    job = repo.add_job(Job(id="job-1", name="Onboard customers"))
    step = repo.add_step(Step(id="step-1", job_id="job-1", name="Prepare", order=1))
    outcome = repo.add_outcome(
        Outcome(id="outcome-1", job_id="job-1", step_id="step-1", statement="Minimize time")
    )
    customer_outcome = repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))

    assert repo.list_jobs() == [job]
    assert repo.get_job("job-1") == job
    assert repo.get_job("missing") is None
    assert repo.get_steps_for_job("job-1") == [step]
    assert repo.get_outcomes("job-1") == [outcome]
    assert repo.get_outcomes("job-1", step_id="step-1") == [outcome]
    assert repo.get_outcomes("job-1", step_id="other") == []
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co-1") == customer_outcome
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("missing") is None
    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes() == [customer_outcome]
    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes("job-1") == [customer_outcome]
    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes("other") == []


def test_snapshot_reloads_every_event_type_from_disk(tmp_path) -> None:
    db_path = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path)
    repo.add_job(Job(id="job-1", name="Onboard customers"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="step-1", job_id="job-1", name="Prepare", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="outcome-1", job_id="job-1", statement="Minimize time"))
    created = repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))
    customer_value = created.customer_value.model_dump()
    customer_value["importance"] = 9.0
    repo.update_customer_outcome("co-1", {"customer_value": customer_value})

    reloaded = SQLiteRepository(db_path)

    assert reloaded.get_job("job-1") is not None
    assert reloaded.get_steps_for_job("job-1")[0].name == "Prepare"
    assert reloaded.get_outcomes("job-1")[0].statement == "Minimize time"
    reloaded_outcome = reloaded.get_customer_outcome("co-1")
    assert reloaded_outcome is not None
    assert reloaded_outcome.customer_value.importance == 9.0


def test_snapshot_drops_customer_outcomes_after_delete_event(tmp_path) -> None:
    db_path = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path)
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))
    assert repo.delete_customer_outcome("co-1") is True

    reloaded = SQLiteRepository(db_path)

    assert reloaded.get_customer_outcome("co-1") is None


def test_snapshot_skips_invalid_update_events(tmp_path) -> None:
    db_path = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path)
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))
    repo.store.append(
        "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED",
        {"id": "co-1", "updates": {"customer_value": {"importance": 99.0}}},
    )

    reloaded = SQLiteRepository(db_path)

    reloaded_outcome = reloaded.get_customer_outcome("co-1")
    assert reloaded_outcome is not None
    assert reloaded_outcome.customer_value.importance == 8.0


def test_update_customer_outcome_returns_none_for_missing_or_invalid(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

    assert repo.update_customer_outcome("missing", {}) is None

    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))
    assert repo.update_customer_outcome("co-1", {"customer_value": {"importance": 99.0}}) is None


def test_delete_customer_outcome_reports_missing_id(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))

    assert repo.delete_customer_outcome("missing") is False


def test_clear_removes_all_entities_and_events(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    repo.add_job(Job(id="job-1", name="Onboard customers"))
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))

    repo.clear()

    assert repo.list_jobs() == []
    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes() == []
    assert repo.store.get_stream() == []


def test_default_path_uses_environment_override(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    db_path = tmp_path / "nested" / "odi.db"
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", str(db_path))

    repo = SQLiteRepository()

    assert db_path.exists()
    assert repo.list_jobs() == []


def test_snapshot_ignores_unknown_event_types(tmp_path) -> None:
    db_path = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path)
    repo.store.append("SOMETHING_ELSE", {"id": "x"})

    reloaded = SQLiteRepository(db_path)

    assert reloaded.list_jobs() == []


def test_closing_the_store_prevents_further_reads(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
    repo.store.close()

    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.ProgrammingError):
        repo.store.get_stream()


def _linked_customer_outcome(id: str, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> CustomerOutcome:
    return CustomerOutcome(
        id=id,
        job_id=job_id,
        step_id=step_id,
        customer_value=CustomerValue(
            direction=Direction.MINIMIZE,
            unit_of_measure="minutes",
            object_of_control="support team",
            statement="Minimize resolution time",
            importance=9.0,
            satisfaction=3.0,
        ),
        business_value=BusinessValue(
            category=BusinessImpactCategory.COST_REDUCTION,
            statement="Reduce support cost",
        ),
    )


def test_round_trips_all_entity_types(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    repo.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job", description="d"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="s1", job_id="j1", name="Step", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(
        Outcome(
            id="o1",
            job_id="j1",
            step_id="s1",
            statement="Min x",
            importance=8.0,
            satisfaction=4.0,
            opportunity_score=12.0,
        )
    )

    reopened = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    assert reopened.get_job("j1").name == "Job"  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    assert reopened.get_step("s1").order == 1  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    assert reopened.get_outcome("o1").opportunity_score == 12.0  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_concurrent_writer_is_visible(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    reader = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    writer = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    writer.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job"))
    assert reader.get_job("j1") is not None  # read-through sees the other connection's write


def test_delete_job_cascades_after_reopen(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    repo.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="s1", job_id="j1", name="Step", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1", statement="Min x"))
    repo.delete_job("j1")

    reopened = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    assert reopened.get_job("j1") is None
    assert reopened.get_step("s1") is None
    assert reopened.get_outcome("o1") is None


def test_update_outcome_persists(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o1", job_id="j1", statement="Min x"))
    repo.update_outcome("o1", {"statement": "Max y", "opportunity_score": 5.0})
    assert SQLiteRepository(db_path=db).get_outcome("o1").statement == "Max y"  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_update_job_and_step_merge_or_return_none_when_missing(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    repo.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="s1", job_id="j1", name="Step", order=1))

    updated_job = repo.update_job("j1", {"name": "Renamed"})
    assert updated_job is not None and updated_job.name == "Renamed"
    updated_step = repo.update_step("s1", {"name": "Renamed step"})
    assert updated_step is not None and updated_step.name == "Renamed step"
    assert repo.update_job("nope", {"name": "x"}) is None
    assert repo.update_step("nope", {"name": "x"}) is None

    reopened = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    assert reopened.get_job("j1").name == "Renamed"  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    assert reopened.get_step("s1").name == "Renamed step"  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def test_delete_missing_returns_false_and_cascade_events_replay(tmp_path):
    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
    repo = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    assert repo.delete_job("nope") is False
    assert repo.delete_step("nope") is False
    assert repo.delete_outcome("nope") is False

    repo.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="s1", job_id="j1", name="Step", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1", statement="Min x"))

    assert repo.delete_outcome("o2") is True

    assert repo.delete_job("j1") is False

    reopened = SQLiteRepository(db_path=db)
    assert reopened.get_step("s1") is None
    assert reopened.get_outcome("o1") is None
    assert reopened.get_outcome("o2") is None
    assert reopened.get_job("j1") is None

"""Tests for the in-memory Repository implementation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from agentic_odi_core.models import (
    BusinessImpactCategory,
    BusinessValue,
    CustomerOutcome,
    CustomerValue,
    Direction,
    Evidence,
    Job,
    Outcome,
    Step,
)
from agentic_odi_core.repository import InMemoryRepository


def _customer_outcome(outcome_id: str, job_id: str = "job-1") -> CustomerOutcome:
    return CustomerOutcome(
        id=outcome_id,
        job_id=job_id,
        customer_value=CustomerValue(
            direction=Direction.MINIMIZE,
            unit_of_measure="minutes",
            object_of_control="time to onboard",
            statement="Minimize the time it takes to onboard",
            importance=8.0,
            satisfaction=4.0,
        ),
        business_value=BusinessValue(
            category=BusinessImpactCategory.COST_REDUCTION,
            statement="Reduce support cost",
        ),
    )


def test_get_outcomes_filters_by_step() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o-1", job_id="job-1", step_id="step-1", statement="one"))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o-2", job_id="job-1", step_id="step-2", statement="two"))

    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes("job-1", step_id="step-1")] == ["o-1"]
    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes("job-1")] == ["o-1", "o-2"]


def test_list_customer_outcomes_without_filter_returns_all() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("co-1", "job-1"))
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("co-2", "job-2"))

    assert [co.id for co in repo.list_customer_outcomes()] == ["co-1", "co-2"]
    assert [co.id for co in repo.list_customer_outcomes("job-2")] == ["co-2"]


def test_update_customer_outcome_returns_none_for_missing_id() -> None:
    assert InMemoryRepository().update_customer_outcome("missing", {}) is None


def test_update_customer_outcome_rejects_invalid_updates() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("co-1"))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        repo.update_customer_outcome("co-1", {"customer_value": {"importance": 99.0}})


def test_delete_customer_outcome_reports_missing_id() -> None:
    assert InMemoryRepository().delete_customer_outcome("missing") is False


def test_clear_removes_all_entities() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    job = repo.add_job(Job(id="job-1", name="Onboard customers"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="step-1", job_id=job.id, name="Prepare", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o-1", job_id=job.id, statement="Minimize time"))
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("co-1", job.id))

    repo.clear()

    assert repo.list_jobs() == []
    assert repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id) == []
    assert repo.get_outcomes(job.id) == []
    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes() == []


def _repo_with_graph() -> InMemoryRepository:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    repo.add_job(Job(id="j1", name="Job"))
    repo.add_step(Step(id="s1", job_id="j1", name="Step", order=1))
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1", statement="Min x"))
    return repo


def _linked_customer_outcome(id: str, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> CustomerOutcome:
    return CustomerOutcome(
        id=id,
        job_id=job_id,
        step_id=step_id,
        customer_value=CustomerValue(
            direction=Direction.MINIMIZE,
            unit_of_measure="minutes",
            object_of_control="support team",
            statement="Minimize resolution time",
            importance=9.0,
            satisfaction=3.0,
        ),
        business_value=BusinessValue(
            category=BusinessImpactCategory.COST_REDUCTION,
            statement="Reduce support cost",
        ),
    )


def test_get_step_and_get_outcome():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    assert repo.get_step("s1").name == "Step"  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    assert repo.get_outcome("o1").statement == "Min x"  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    assert repo.get_step("missing") is None


def test_update_job_merges_and_returns_none_when_missing():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    updated = repo.update_job("j1", {"name": "Renamed"})
    assert updated is not None and updated.name == "Renamed"
    assert repo.update_job("nope", {"name": "x"}) is None


def test_delete_job_cascades_dependents():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    assert repo.delete_job("j1") is True
    assert repo.get_job("j1") is None
    assert repo.get_step("s1") is None
    assert repo.get_outcome("o1") is None
    assert repo.delete_job("j1") is False


def test_delete_step_cascades_its_outcomes():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o2", job_id="j1", statement="Unbound"))
    assert repo.delete_step("s1") is True
    assert repo.get_step("s1") is None
    assert repo.get_outcome("o1") is None
    assert repo.get_outcome("o2") is not None


def test_update_step_and_update_outcome_merge_or_return_none():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    updated_step = repo.update_step("s1", {"name": "Renamed step"})
    assert updated_step is not None and updated_step.name == "Renamed step"
    updated_outcome = repo.update_outcome("o1", {"statement": "Max y"})
    assert updated_outcome is not None and updated_outcome.statement == "Max y"
    assert repo.update_step("nope", {"name": "x"}) is None
    assert repo.update_outcome("nope", {"statement": "x"}) is None


def test_delete_outcome_and_delete_step_return_false_when_missing():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    assert repo.delete_outcome("nope") is False
    assert repo.delete_step("nope") is False
    assert repo.delete_outcome("o1") is True
    assert repo.get_outcome("o1") is None


def test_delete_job_cascades_customer_outcomes():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_linked_customer_outcome("co1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1"))
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_linked_customer_outcome("co2", job_id="other"))
    assert repo.delete_job("j1") is True
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co1") is None
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co2") is not None


def test_delete_step_cascades_customer_outcomes():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_linked_customer_outcome("co1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1"))
    repo.add_customer_outcome(_linked_customer_outcome("co2", job_id="j1"))
    assert repo.delete_step("s1") is True
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co1") is None
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co2") is not None
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co1") is None
    assert repo.get_customer_outcome("co2") is not None


def _evidence(id: str, **overrides) -> Evidence:
    payload = {
        "id": id,
        "source_name": "gong",
        "source_kind": "mcp",
        "item_type": "resource",
        "name": "feedback",
        "content": "Lost hours on deploy",
    }
    payload.update(overrides)
    return Evidence(**payload)


def test_evidence_crud_and_filters():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1", outcome_id="o1"))
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e2", job_id="j1"))
    assert repo.get_evidence("e1") is not None
    assert len(repo.list_evidence(job_id="j1")) == 2
    assert [item.id for item in repo.list_evidence(step_id="s1")] == ["e1"]
    assert [item.id for item in repo.list_evidence(outcome_id="o1")] == ["e1"]
    assert repo.delete_evidence("e1") is True
    assert repo.delete_evidence("e1") is False
    assert repo.get_evidence("e1") is None


def test_delete_job_cascades_evidence():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e1", job_id="j1", step_id="s1", outcome_id="o1"))
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e2", job_id="j1"))
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e3", job_id="other"))
    assert repo.delete_job("j1") is True
    assert repo.get_evidence("e1") is None
    assert repo.get_evidence("e2") is None
    assert repo.get_evidence("e3") is not None


def test_delete_outcome_cascades_evidence():
    repo = _repo_with_graph()
    repo.add_evidence(_evidence("e1", job_id="j1", outcome_id="o1"))
    assert repo.delete_outcome("o1") is True
    assert repo.get_evidence("e1") is None

"""Pagination on the list methods of both repositories and the service layer."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from agentic_odi_core.models import (
    BusinessValue,
    CustomerOutcome,
    CustomerValue,
    Evidence,
    Job,
    Outcome,
    Step,
)
from agentic_odi_core.repository import InMemoryRepository, page
from agentic_odi_core.services import ODIService
from agentic_odi_core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository


def _customer_value(index: int) -> CustomerValue:
    return CustomerValue(
        direction="minimize",
        unit_of_measure="minutes",
        object_of_control="lead time",
        statement=f"co{index}",
        importance=7.0,
        satisfaction=3.0,
    )


def _business_value(index: int) -> BusinessValue:
    return BusinessValue(
        category="operational_efficiency",
        statement=f"bv{index}",
    )


def test_page_slices_and_defaults_to_everything() -> None:
    items = list(range(10))

    assert page(items) == items
    assert page(items, 3) == [0, 1, 2]
    assert page(items, 3, 2) == [2, 3, 4]
    assert page(items, 3, 9) == [9]
    assert page(items, 3, 99) == []


def test_page_rejects_negative_values() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        page([1, 2, 3], 1, -1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        page([1, 2, 3], -1, 0)


def _seed(repo) -> tuple[Job, list[Step]]:
    job = repo.add_job(Job(name="Deploy", description="Ship a service"))
    steps = [
        repo.add_step(Step(id=f"STEP-{i}", job_id=job.id, name=f"step {i}", order=i))
        for i in range(5)
    ]
    for i, step in enumerate(steps):
        repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id=f"OUT-{i}", job_id=job.id, step_id=step.id, statement=f"o{i}"))
        repo.add_customer_outcome(
            CustomerOutcome(
                id=f"CO-{i}",
                job_id=job.id,
                step_id=step.id,
                customer_value=_customer_value(i),
                business_value=_business_value(i),
            )
        )
        repo.add_evidence(
            Evidence(
                id=f"EV-{i}",
                source_name="Gong",
                source_kind="manual",
                name=f"evidence {i}",
                content=f"evidence {i}",
                job_id=job.id,
                step_id=step.id,
                outcome_id=f"OUT-{i}",
            )
        )
    return job, steps


def test_inmemory_repository_paginates_each_list() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    job, steps = _seed(repo)

    assert len(repo.list_jobs()) == 1
    assert repo.list_jobs(limit=0) == []

    all_steps = repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id)
    assert len(all_steps) == 5
    assert repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id, limit=2) == all_steps[:2]
    assert repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id, limit=2, offset=4) == all_steps[4:]

    assert len(repo.get_outcomes(job.id)) == 5
    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes(job.id, limit=2, offset=1)] == ["OUT-1", "OUT-2"]
    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes(job.id, steps[0].id, limit=1)] == ["OUT-0"]

    assert len(repo.list_customer_outcomes(job.id)) == 5
    assert [c.id for c in repo.list_customer_outcomes(job.id, limit=2, offset=3)] == [
        "CO-3",
        "CO-4",
    ]

    assert len(repo.list_evidence(job_id=job.id)) == 5
    assert [e.id for e in repo.list_evidence(job_id=job.id, limit=2, offset=2)] == ["EV-2", "EV-3"]
    assert [e.id for e in repo.list_evidence(step_id=steps[1].id, limit=1)] == ["EV-1"]


def test_sqlite_repository_paginates_each_list(tmp_path) -> None:
    repo = SQLiteRepository(str(tmp_path / "page.db"))
    job, _steps = _seed(repo)

    assert len(repo.list_jobs()) == 1
    assert repo.list_jobs(limit=1) == repo.list_jobs()[:1]
    assert repo.list_jobs(limit=1, offset=1) == []

    assert len(repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id)) == 5
    assert len(repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id, limit=2, offset=4)) == 1

    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes(job.id, limit=2, offset=2)] == ["OUT-2", "OUT-3"]
    assert [c.id for c in repo.list_customer_outcomes(limit=2, offset=2)] == ["CO-2", "CO-3"]
    assert [e.id for e in repo.list_evidence(job_id=job.id, limit=2, offset=2)] == [
        "EV-2",
        "EV-3",
    ]


def test_service_pages_job_map_in_step_order() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    service = ODIService(repo)
    job = service.add_job(name="Deploy")

    # Insert out of order: pagination must still return ascending order.
    for order in (3, 0, 4, 1, 2):
        service.add_step(job_id=job.id, name=f"step {order}", order=order)

    full = service.get_job_map(job.id)
    assert [s.order for s in full] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert [s.order for s in service.get_job_map(job.id, limit=2)] == [0, 1]
    assert [s.order for s in service.get_job_map(job.id, limit=2, offset=3)] == [3, 4]


def test_service_passes_pagination_through() -> None:
    repo = InMemoryRepository()
    service = ODIService(repo)
    job = service.add_job(name="Deploy")
    for i in range(3):
        step = service.add_step(job_id=job.id, name=f"step {i}", order=i)
        service.add_customer_outcome(
            job_id=job.id,
            customer_value=_customer_value(i),
            business_value=_business_value(i),
            step_id=step.id,
        )
        service.add_evidence(
            source_name="Gong",
            source_kind="manual",
            name=f"evidence {i}",
            content=f"evidence {i}",
            job_id=job.id,
            step_id=step.id,
        )

    assert len(service.get_jobs()) == 1
    assert service.get_jobs(limit=1, offset=1) == []
    assert len(service.list_customer_outcomes(limit=1)) == 1
    assert len(service.list_evidence(limit=1, offset=2)) == 1
    assert service.list_evidence(limit=1, offset=3) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_kwargs", [{"limit": -1}, {"offset": -1}])
def test_service_surfaces_invalid_pages(bad_kwargs: dict) -> None:
    service = ODIService(InMemoryRepository())
    job = service.add_job(name="Deploy")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        service.get_jobs(**bad_kwargs)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        service.get_job_map(job.id, **bad_kwargs)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        service.list_evidence(**bad_kwargs)

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest
from agentic_odi_mcp_server import mcp
from fastmcp import Client


def _json(text: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads(text)


def _payload(text: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads(text.split(": ", 1)[1])


async def _new_job(client) -> str:
    res = await client.call_tool("add_job", {"name": "Onboard customers"})
    return _payload(res.content[0].text)["id"]  # type: ignore[index]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_tool_catalog_exposes_context_and_evidence_tools():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        names = {tool.name for tool in await client.list_tools()}

    assert {
        "get_job_map",
        "evaluate_outcome",
        "get_odi_schema",
        "add_evidence",
        "list_evidence",
        "promote_evidence",
    } <= names
    assert "greet" not in names


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_evaluate_outcome_accepts_well_formed_statement():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        res = await client.call_tool(
            "evaluate_outcome",
            {"statement": "Minimize the time to onboard a customer when they sign up"},
        )

        result = _json(res.content[0].text)  # type: ignore[index]

    assert result["valid"] is True
    assert result["direction"] == "minimize"
    assert result["issues"] == []


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_evaluate_outcome_reports_format_issues():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        res = await client.call_tool("evaluate_outcome", {"statement": "Make it better"})

        result = _json(res.content[0].text)  # type: ignore[index]

    assert result["valid"] is False
    assert result["direction"] is None
    assert any("Minimize" in issue for issue in result["issues"])
    assert any("context" in issue.lower() for issue in result["issues"])


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_evaluate_outcome_includes_existing_job_outcomes():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        job_id = await _new_job(client)
        await client.call_tool(
            "add_outcome",
            {"job_id": job_id, "statement": "Minimize time to first value"},
        )

        res = await client.call_tool(
            "evaluate_outcome",
            {
                "statement": "Maximize the share of customers reaching first value when onboarding",
                "job_id": job_id,
            },
        )
        result = _json(res.content[0].text)  # type: ignore[index]

    assert result["job_id"] == job_id
    assert result["existing_outcomes"][0]["statement"] == "Minimize time to first value"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_get_odi_schema_returns_every_entity():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        res = await client.call_tool("get_odi_schema", {})
        schema = _json(res.content[0].text)  # type: ignore[index]

    assert {"Job", "Step", "Outcome", "CustomerOutcome", "Evidence"} <= set(schema)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_evidence_lifecycle_over_mcp():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        job_id = await _new_job(client)
        created = await client.call_tool(
            "add_evidence",
            {
                "source_name": "gong",
                "source_kind": "mcp",
                "item_type": "resource",
                "name": "feedback",
                "content": "Onboarding took two hours",
                "job_id": job_id,
            },
        )
        evidence_id = _payload(created.content[0].text)["id"]  # type: ignore[index]

        listed = await client.call_tool("list_evidence", {"job_id": job_id})
        assert evidence_id in listed.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]

        fetched = await client.call_tool("get_evidence", {"evidence_id": evidence_id})
        assert "Onboarding took two hours" in fetched.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]

        promoted = await client.call_tool(
            "promote_evidence",
            {
                "evidence_id": evidence_id,
                "target": "outcome",
                "job_id": job_id,
                "statement": "Minimize the time to onboard a customer when signing up",
                "importance": 8,
                "satisfaction": 4,
            },
        )
        assert "Outcome created successfully" in promoted.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]
        assert '"opportunity_score":12.0' in promoted.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]

        deleted = await client.call_tool("delete_evidence", {"evidence_id": evidence_id})
        assert "deleted successfully" in deleted.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_evidence_tools_report_not_found():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        missing = "no-such-evidence"
        assert (
            "not found"
            in (await client.call_tool("get_evidence", {"evidence_id": missing})).content[0].text
        )  # type: ignore[index]
        assert (
            "not found"
            in (await client.call_tool("delete_evidence", {"evidence_id": missing})).content[0].text
        )  # type: ignore[index]
